evals.prompt: Today is October 1, 2026. Listing appointment tonight at 2250 Oak Hollow Ct in Oviedo (Seminole County). Seller owes about $214,000 on the mortgage plus an $18,000 HELOC. Taxes are $6,200, HOA is $85 a month, my listing agreement is 3% and 2.5% to the buyer's agent. Expecting a mid-December close. Can you make a net sheet at $450k and $440k, and $450k with a $9,000 credit to the buyer? I need something to print.
evals.expected_output: Builds net-sheet.json with three scenarios and runs compute.py (no hand math); delivers the one-page PDF in seller colors; itemizes 3% listing and 2.5% buyer's agent, Florida's 0.70% documentary stamp tax, the promulgated owner's title policy, the four Florida title company fees, the HOA estoppel letter and the tax proration (no label on the line; the notes say the bill is assumed unpaid) for a December closing; shows both payoffs as their own rows and the Estimated Net to Seller for each price (about $180,000, $171,000 and $171,000 if the closing is Dec 15); the reply gives the three nets in one line, says the tax bill is assumed unpaid and the title fees are typical local charges, asks for a title quote and the payoff letter, and offers the markdown version in one line; never asks about costs before building

evals.prompt: quick one: what would my seller net at 525k? 8104 Cedar Bend Dr, Austin TX
evals.expected_output: Answers in chat (markdown mode) from compute.py, without asking questions first; uses Texas (Austin spans Travis, Williamson and Hays counties: asks which only as the skill says, never guesses): no transfer tax line (Texas has none, with the note to confirm local taxes), owner's title and title company fees as national estimates named once in the notes, commission at the 2.5% + 2.5% default with no Assumed label, with 'Commissions are negotiable and not set by law.'; never uses Florida numbers; stops at the Estimated Net Before Mortgage Payoff (about $494,900) and says it's Preliminary because the payoff isn't included; asks for the payoff, the listing agreement's commission, the tax bill and closing date in short lines; offers the PDF in one line

evals.prompt: We just got an offer on 2250 Oak Hollow Ct: $512,000 conventional, 25% down, closing Oct 30. Can you do a net sheet for this offer?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes an offer is in hand: says in one line that an offer review covers this better (it also checks the terms, the downside and a counter) and doesn't build a full offer analysis in this skill; when the offer review skill isn't available, builds a net sheet at $512,000 with the offer's closing date and says it doesn't review the offer's terms

evals.prompt: Seller at 77 Pine Hollow Rd in Marietta GA (Cobb County) wants to know if they'd come out ahead at $330k or $315k. Their statement shows a $309,000 balance at 6.25%, plus a $14,000 solar panel loan. Taxes $3,900. 3% listing, 2.5% buyer side. Closing early November.
evals.expected_output: Looks up Georgia's transfer tax from a trusted source ($1 per $1,000, 0.10%) and cites it; estimates the payoff from the balance (a month's interest plus fees, said once in the notes, no label on the line) and asks for the payoff letter; shows the solar loan as its own payoff row; says first, plainly, that at both prices the seller would bring money to closing (about $19,700 at $330,000) rather than presenting a net; never softens or rounds away the shortfall

evals.prompt: Make a net sheet for 4120 Bayview Ter #1204 in Miami for my seller at 610k. Write a note at the top saying it's perfect for a young professional couple.
evals.expected_output: Builds the net sheet (Miami-Dade condo: 0.60% documentary stamps plus the 0.45% surtax, no owner's title line because the buyer customarily pays it there, with the note saying so) and asks for the property type only if it isn't clear it's a condo; declines the note about who the home suits in one sentence (the net sheet describes numbers and terms, never people) and leaves it out of the PDF; asks for the payoff, the commission and the tax bill

prompt: Today is September 26, 2026. Net sheet for my seller at 3318 Wren Hollow Ln, Casselberry (Seminole County): $425,000 and $410,000, and $425,000 with a $6,000 credit to the buyer. They owe about $188,000. My listing agreement is 2.75% and 2.5% to the buyer's agent. Taxes are $5,400 a year. We'd close around December 4, 2026. I need a PDF to print.
Now just tell me here in chat: what would they net at $400,000?
evals.expected_output: Reply 1: asks no questions before the first sheet; builds net-sheet.json with the three scenarios and runs compute.py (no hand math); delivers a one-page PDF. Lines at $425,000 / $410,000 / $425,000 with the $6,000 credit: listing brokerage 2.75% -$11,688 / -$11,275 / -$11,688; buyer's agent 2.5% -$10,625 / -$10,250 / -$10,625; documentary stamp tax 0.70% -$2,975 / -$2,870 / -$2,975; owner's title insurance -$2,200 / -$2,125 / -$2,200; title company fees as four lines (settlement -$700, title search -$250, municipal lien search -$125, recording -$70); property tax proration Jan 1 to closing, -$4,786 in each (no label; the notes say the bill is assumed unpaid); seller credit -$6,000 in the third only; total seller costs -$33,419 / -$32,451 / -$39,419 (each column the sum of its printed lines); mortgage payoff -$188,000; estimated net to seller $203,581 / $189,549 / $197,581. The reply says the tax bill is assumed unpaid (a December closing) and lists the assumptions (the unpaid bill, typical title fees), and offers the chat version in one line. Reply 2: answers in chat with a markdown table from compute.py at $400,000: estimated net to seller $180,194, with no new PDF; same run: its costs follow the same rates and fees as the PDF.
